one_liner: DataForSEO is a data provider offering REST APIs for SERP data, keyword research, backlinks, on-page/domain analytics, and business/local data.
self_serve_evidence: Users create a free account and immediately get login/password API credentials from the dashboard, no sales contact required.
api_surface: Broad REST API family covering SERP, Keywords Data, Domain Analytics, Backlinks, On-Page, Business Data, App Data, and Content/AI Optimization endpoints, with client libraries in multiple languages.
existing_mcp_detail: Official DataForSEO MCP server (dataforseo.com/model-context-protocol), also listed on PulseMCP; several community MCP wrappers exist too.
notes: Simple, well-documented Basic Auth (base64 login:password) makes this one of the easier integrations; pricing is pay-as-you-go per API call.

one_liner: SE Ranking is an SEO platform (rank tracking, keyword/backlink/domain research, site audits) exposed via a Data API and a Project API.
self_serve_evidence: Any active subscription plan can generate an API key instantly from the API Dashboard, with no sales gate for standard access (enterprise volume needs sales).
api_surface: REST API with two surfaces (Data API and Project API) sharing one token; broad coverage of keyword research, backlinks, domain analysis, and rank tracking/project management.
existing_mcp_detail: Official centrally-hosted MCP server at api.seranking.com/mcp exposing 160+ tools, using OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration; also ships 7 Claude Skills.
notes: Core REST API uses simple Token-header API-key auth; the newer official MCP server layers OAuth 2.1 on top for agent access specifically.

one_liner: Ahrefs is an SEO toolset (Site Explorer, keyword research, rank tracking, backlink analysis) that exposes a REST API v3.
self_serve_evidence: API v3 access does not require an Enterprise plan or sales contact — it's available self-serve to Lite-tier and higher subscribers, with free test queries available before subscribing.
api_surface: REST API with a published OpenAPI spec; covers Site Explorer, keyword data, backlinks, rank tracking, and brand/AI-visibility monitoring; usage metered in API 'units' per plan.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Ahrefs MCP server (github.com/ahrefs/ahrefs-mcp-server; docs.ahrefs.com/en/mcp), also listed on PulseMCP.
notes: Requires an underlying paid Lite+ subscription (not free-tier), but that's a normal commercial gate, not a sales/approval gate.

one_liner: MrScraper is a smaller web-scraping SaaS offering a Google SERP scraper plus scrapers for e-commerce/travel marketplaces (Shopee, TikTok, Lazada, Booking.com, etc.).
self_serve_evidence: Docs reference a self-service dashboard (app.mrscraper.com) where users manage API tokens and usage; no sales-contact language found.
api_surface: REST API with sync and async Google SERP scraping endpoints, an async-result-retrieval endpoint, and additional vertical scrapers (marketplaces, travel, jobs); relatively narrow/niche compared to Apify/Bright Data.
existing_mcp_detail: No official or community MCP server found for MrScraper specifically.
blocker: It's a small, sparsely-documented vendor (docs.mrscraper.com has limited public detail on rate limits, pricing tiers, and full endpoint catalog) — genuinely obscure as flagged, so confidence in completeness is lower than the larger players.
notes: Real product with real docs (confirmed via docs.mrscraper.com), not fabricated, but it is a much smaller/lesser-known player than the other scraping vendors in this set, and no MCP ecosystem exists around it yet.

one_liner: Apify is a web-scraping and automation platform ('Actors') with a large marketplace of ready-made scrapers/crawlers accessible via REST API.
self_serve_evidence: Free account signup with self-serve API token generation in Apify Console; usage-based/free-tier pricing, no sales gate.
api_surface: Broad REST API covering Actor discovery/execution, dataset/key-value-store/log storage access, and thousands of community/first-party Actors (scrapers) as callable tools.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Apify MCP server hosted at mcp.apify.com, open-source at github.com/apify/apify-mcp-server, supports OAuth or bearer-token auth.
notes: One of the most agent-ready platforms researched; official MCP explicitly excludes full-permission and rental Actors for security/billing reasons.

one_liner: Firecrawl converts websites into clean, LLM-ready data via scrape/crawl/extract/search REST endpoints.
self_serve_evidence: Users generate an API key instantly at firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys; docs even describe an instant 'keyless' quick-start path with no signup required for trial use.
api_surface: REST API covering scrape, crawl, map, extract, and search operations; moderately broad and purpose-built for feeding LLMs/agents.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Firecrawl MCP server (github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server), documented at docs.firecrawl.dev/mcp-server.
notes: Explicitly designed for AI-agent consumption (LLM-ready markdown/JSON output), making it one of the most natural agent-toolkit fits in the set.

one_liner: Bright Data is a large web-data infrastructure platform offering proxies, a Web Unlocker, SERP API, Scraping Browser, and pre-built Scrapers.
self_serve_evidence: Signup and initial API access are immediate/self-serve with a free trial and recurring free tier, but full access to Proxy Networks and Web Unlocker is restricted until a payment method is verified.
api_surface: Broad REST API surface spanning Web Unlocker, SERP API, Scraping Browser, pre-built Scrapers, Functions, and a scraper Marketplace, with permission-scoped API keys (Admin/Finance/Ops/Limit/User).
existing_mcp_detail: Official Bright Data MCP server at github.com/brightdata/brightdata-mcp (also an official CLI at github.com/brightdata/cli); several community forks also exist.
blocker: Certain high-value products (Proxy Networks, Web Unlocker) require payment-method verification before full access, adding an onboarding step beyond pure self-serve.
notes: Large, mature API surface; the official MCP server and CLI both suggest strong agent-readiness despite the payment-verification friction.

one_liner: Sherlock is a free, open-source Python command-line tool that hunts for a given username across 400+ social networks.
self_serve_evidence: Anyone can freely install it (pipx/Docker/package managers) and run it locally with no account, API key, or approval needed — but this is 'self-serve software install', not a hosted API signup.
api_surface: None. There is no hosted REST/GraphQL API — it's a local CLI/Python tool that queries each social platform directly and writes results to local files. A 2020-era GitHub issue proposed wrapping it as a REST API but this was never merged into the core project.
existing_mcp_detail: Unofficial community MCP wrapper exists (FastMCP-based subprocess wrapper), not affiliated with the sherlock-project maintainers.
blocker: No official hosted API exists to call — building an agent-toolkit integration means self-hosting/wrapping the CLI tool (subprocess execution, containerization, rate-limiting against target social sites yourself) rather than calling a vendor endpoint.
notes: Confirmed via the project's own README: it is explicitly a local CLI tool, not a SaaS/hosted API. Also carries legal/ethical/ToS risk since it queries third-party sites directly.

one_liner: Waterfall.io is a B2B contact/company data platform for finding and enriching contacts, prospecting by title/company, and verifying emails (a 'waterfall' enrichment provider, à la a Clay alternative).
self_serve_evidence: Docs describe a straightforward x-api-key header auth scheme against api.waterfall.io with full public endpoint documentation, implying self-service key issuance rather than sales gating, though the docs don't state this explicitly.
api_surface: REST API with roughly 13 documented endpoints split into synchronous (contact/company search, email verification, job-change detection, company reveal, admin/reporting) and asynchronous (prospecting, contact/phone/company enrichment) categories.
existing_mcp_detail: No official or community MCP server found for Waterfall.io itself.
notes: This is a genuinely small/niche vendor as flagged — docs.waterfall.io does exist and is real (confirmed live), but pricing/self-serve signup flow could not be independently confirmed beyond the API auth documentation itself, so confidence is medium rather than high.

one_liner: Clay is a go-to-market data/enrichment platform ('spreadsheet-like' tables) that combines 100+ data providers and AI agents for prospecting, enrichment, and outreach workflows, and now also exposes its own public API.
self_serve_evidence: Clay's own public API (Searches/Routines), launched July 2026, is self-serve via an API key on every plan including legacy ones, but the 'Tables' read primitive is Enterprise-plan only.
api_surface: REST-style public API (clay-api-key header) with inbound primitives — Searches (query Clay's database), Routines (run packaged workflow logic, async with polling/webhooks), and Tables (Enterprise-only read access) — plus a separate outbound HTTP API integration feature inside tables for calling arbitrary third-party APIs.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Clay MCP server built by Clay Labs Inc., exposing 150+ data providers/agents/workflows into ChatGPT, Claude, and Codex.
notes: Clay historically had no true outbound public API; this changed with a July 2026 public API/CLI/agent-plugin launch, which the official MCP server and this dataset should reflect as a recent but now-solid agent-integration surface.
